title: The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets
abstract: arXiv:2611.24971v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) improves large language model performance at inference time without updating model parameters. However, these gains are not free: in practical deployments, longer prompts directly increase inference cost and latency. Under a fixed token budget, prompt construction therefore becomes a resource-allocation problem. While prior work has often focused on how many examples to include in ICL, we study the complementary question of whether the available budget is better spent on a few long demonstrations or on a larger number of shorter ones. We study this aspect in question answering (QA), by organizing candidate demonstrations into length-based bins and constructing prompts from examples within the same length range under fixed budgets. translated_title: 小示例的投资回报率：Token预算下的上下文学习优化
translated_abstract: 上下文学习（ICL）无需更新模型参数即可提升大语言模型在推理阶段的性能。然而，这些收益并非没有代价：在实际部署中，更长的提示词会直接增加推理成本和延迟。因此，在固定的Token预算下，提示词构建成为一个资源分配问题。虽然先前的工作大多关注ICL中应包含多少个示例，我们研究了与之互补的问题：可用的预算是更好地花费在少量长示例上，还是花费在更多短示例上。我们在问答（QA）任务中研究这一问题，将候选示例按长度分桶，并在固定预算下从相同长度范围内的示例构建提示词。在两个问答基准（Beat the AI 和 Natural Questions）上，使用六个指令微调的大语言模型进行的实验表明，较短的示例通常是最有效的……
tldr: 该论文发现在固定Token预算下，将预算用于更多较短的示例而非少量较长示例，能在问答任务中实现更优的上下文学习效果。
en_tdlr: Under fixed token budgets, allocating the budget to a larger number of shorter demonstrations rather than fewer longer ones generally yields better in-context learning performance in question answering tasks.
